newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-VETERAN JOHNSON TELLS NASEEM TO GROW UP.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-VETERAN JOHNSON TELLS NASEEM TO GROW UP.

text.p: Veteran world featherweight champion Tom "Boom Boom" Johnson showed his maturity on Thursday when he refused to rise to the taunts of "Prince" Naseem Hamed and told the young British boxer to grow up.
"We have come here to put on a fight, and we have come here to go home champion of the world. Anything that is said outside that, really is hype," the 32-year-old American said.
Johnson said the fact two world champions were stepping into the ring together and one would emerge double world champion was all the hype that was needed.
"Grow up, kid. You don't need to hype up this one," he said.
The bout at the London Arena on Saturday will unify the World Boxing Organisation (WBO) title, held by Naseem, and the International Boxing Federation (IBF) belt, held by Johnson.
The American has won 44 of his 48 fights and defended his IBF title 11 times. Naseem is unbeaten in 24 bouts and defended his WBO belt four times, but this clash will be his toughest test yet.

The flamboyant 22-year-old Naseem was as cocky as ever during the press conference. He lolled in his chair, tapped the microphone while Johnson answered questions, and did his best to get a rise out of the veteran and his camp.
"I've already won," Naseem said. "I've just got to turn up."

"This is war, this is the Brits versus America, and the Brits are going to come out on top, with the Arab world," said Naseem who has a huge following in his parents' native country Yemen, although he was born and bred in Sheffield, in England's industrial heartland..
"I'm predicting this fight in the third round and I'm dedicating it to my mother, 'cos she predicted the fight. She wants a bit of entertainment and then she wants a knockout.,"
The Briton said he would knock the American out in the third round.
Johnson admitted he saw Naseem as a definite threat, but throughout the jibes and boasts, the American sat with a wide grin on his face.
"I know that you know, you're doing your usual. You want to hype up the media," he said calmly. "Save your energy son, you're going to need it."
Johnson warmed up to the traditional pre-bout verbal sparring when Naseem urged him to put his purse on the line and accept his winner take all offer.

"We can do that if you like, but I tell you we go to these rules: We'll alleviate (do without) the referee, we'll alleviate the officials, we'll take off the gloves and we'll fight to the death," the American said.
"You will be in worse trouble," Naseem responded. "I will have to knock you out in one round...you might not even get back to America...You'll be in the graveyard."

The last comment drew some sharp intakes of breath, and Johnson's trainer Duke Durden said: "That's enough". Fight promoter Frank Warren was quick to step in to add it would be a fair fight, with gloves on.
Naseem continued to goad Johnson and his camp, saying: "Hype it up, hype it up."
"I don't need hype. I know why I'm here," Johnson said as the fighters left the press conference. "I'm here to win."
